method: Independent expanded-power composition and 64-subinterval Bernstein convex-hull bounds for each derivative polynomial; 1e-9 numerical pad. This is floating-point algebra, not directed interval arithmetic.
mathematical_review: On each inverse-knot clock interval, q composed with the quintic clock has degree at most15. Time derivatives divide by interval width and duration once per order.
Endpoint plus all real derivative roots gives extrema of absolute rates; recursive derivative-root isolation covers monotone intervals and retains repeated stationary roots as extra candidates.
Both sides of all cubic junctions are evaluated, and malformed/nonfinite/visible C0-C2 discontinuities reject.
Duration rescaling changes velocity by 1/T and acceleration by 1/T^2; the original1.002 factor remains.
The test validates command-reference rates. Physical measured rates, soft contacts, rigid clearance and future reobserved insertion still require existing separate gates.
limitations: Double-precision root isolation and1.002 margin are a numerical algorithm, not a proof for arbitrary ill-conditioned adversarial polynomials.
Permitted C0/C1/C2 numerical junction tolerances are not exact continuity proofs; source production paths are scipy CubicSpline.
Changing duration alters the future native deformable state; previous frozen route success is not transferable to a new run.
